A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, algorithms, and appendices are readable, and retained material can be matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic-bandit and MovieLens-derived recommendation experiments, including appendix results on rank recovery and ground-truth subspaces.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical experiments and adds Thompson-sampling comparisons, oracle-feature comparisons, and offline-sample-size analyses.

M1.justification: v2 adds ProBALL-TS (Appendix G, Algorithm 5), extending the method family to posterior sampling using low- and high-dimensional Gaussian posteriors. SOLD, LOCAL-UCB, and ProBALL-UCB remain unchanged. The pseudoinverse SOLD variant was already used in v1; its new pseudocode is additional documentation.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate synthetic linear latent bandits and the same MovieLens-1M-derived recommendation task. Added oracle-feature controls and sample-size sweeps change experimental configurations, not dataset, population, or task coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds evaluated TS, mmTS, and MixTS baselines in the MovieLens comparisons, substantially broadening comparison beyond LinUCB, mUCB, and mmUCB. The 'Perfect' reference curve in v1 Figure 8 is also absent from the corresponding SOLD-based rating comparison in v2 Figure 9.

E3.justification: The existing simulation and MovieLens settings are retained. New evaluation designs vary offline sample counts, compare against algorithms supplied with low-dimensional ground-truth features, and measure Frobenius subspace error alongside regret at T = 200 (Appendix H.3.3–H.4).

E4.justification: v2 adds oracle-feature comparisons and systematic sample-complexity analyses connecting offline sample count to subspace error and downstream regret. It also examines ProBALL-TS across tuning choices. Rank recovery, UCB tuning sweeps, and initializing ProBALL-UCB with ground-truth subspaces already appeared in v1.

E5.justification: Both versions use 30 trials and one-standard-error bands. v2 Figure 2 newly specifies fresh latent states across trials for every summary panel, including the synthetic experiment; v1's synthetic Figure 2 only specified 30 trials. This clarifies reporting without establishing additional runs.

E6.justification: v2 adds Thompson-sampling results, oracle-feature results, and sample-size curves showing declining subspace error and small-τ regret approaching oracle performance. Matched MovieLens UCB curves also change (v1 Figure 3; v2 Figure 8). The new Figure 10 shows MixTS outperforming ProBALL-TS at larger τ, despite its blanket superiority caption.

T1.justification: v2 adds a claimed matching regret lower bound: informal Theorem 3, formal Theorem 7, and Appendix F's parameter constructions, change-of-measure arguments, and regime analysis. The original upper-bound proofs and de Finetti results are substantially retained, including material moved between the main text and appendices.

C1.justification: v1 presents minimax guarantees as future work. v2's abstract and introduction instead claim LOCAL-UCB is minimax optimal and identify the matching lower bound as a principal contribution. The original subspace-learning, acceleration, and de Finetti claims remain.

C2.justification: v2 explains SOLD's correction matrices through ridge-regularization distortion, where v1 emphasized unseen actions, and separately discusses pseudoinverse distortion. It also interprets the new oracle and sample-size comparisons as showing little loss from estimating the subspace when sufficient offline data and small τ are used.

D1.justification: Algorithm 4 explicitly documents the previously used pseudoinverse SOLD implementation, including its eigenvector-based correction matrices. Most experimental hyperparameters, preprocessing, hardware, and runtime information are retained or relocated to Appendix H; no new code-access location is provided.

R1.justification: v2 substantially revises positioning around latent bandits, meta/multitask learning, and hybrid reinforcement learning. It adds comparisons with Hong et al. (2022), Cella et al. (2022), Yang et al. (2022), and Cai et al. (2024), among others, while removing earlier discussions such as Tennenholtz et al. (2021). It also claims the first hybrid offline-online lower bound.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are extensively rewritten, and 'Contextual' is added to the title. The de Finetti discussion moves from Section 2 to Section 8, experimental details move into an organized Appendix H, method explanations are rewritten, and a contents section is added.

P2.justification: v2 replaces the separate main experimental figures with a four-panel overview, reorganizes retained plots in the appendices, and adds Thompson-sampling, oracle-feature, and sample-complexity displays. It also adds algorithm boxes, enlarges the geometric illustration, and changes the document's text width and layout.

improvement.justification: The added experiments, explicit implementation details, and clearer organization improve evidence and usability. However, the newly central minimax claim has an unresolved proof problem: Appendix F.3's regret equality uses a comparator of norm sqrt(2), although Theorem 7 restricts actions to the unit ball. Figure 10 also claims universal superiority over MixTS despite contrary larger-τ curves. These substantive reliability concerns prevent a confident net quality judgment.
